question: The control: is the chat untouched?
why: Mickey's three arms (23:10 to 24:37) and "remember everything, see what mistakes it makes". The no-personalization arm is the control the other two are read against.
source: wiki/meta/spec-2026-11-10-la-personalization-lab-test-tree.md, heading "Aspect `aggressiveness`: none, light or aggressive?", row `none`
hypothesis: Yes: with personalization off every prompt equals main's prompt byte for byte, and no profile table is written.
cost_estimate: none: no model call (the three runs are deterministic replays; the lab's live command makes one headless calibration call per invocation, which this case never uses)

deviations.from: test tree row: `syn2` replayed with personalization off
deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized) and Amendment A2 maps the row's `syn2` bars onto it: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas. The case is deterministic, so per A2 it replays all 188 personas of anon-personas (no seeded sample). syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside and never alone. Results on anon-personas are numbers only (counts and ratios).

The prompts are built by the branch's own `build_turn_prompt` with the production off-path (gate.resolve, then runtime.profile_for_request, with the profile store replaced by a store that counts every write call) and compared with the same prompt built by `build_prompt` from `git show config.main_ref:server/chat/V2/prompts/prompt_fragments.py`, loaded in an isolated module namespace. The core prompt, summary and page url are fixed synthetic strings (the real core prompt lives in Braintrust); summary and page url are switched on for fixed turn positions so every branch of the builder is compared. byte_identical_off and store_writes are the core's counted metrics, read from the replay's diagnostics. Prompt hashes (SHA-256 of both prompts, per turn) are kept in the replay's diagnostics and are not part of the result files; no prompt text is stored anywhere.
